dichXuoi.en: Learning is as deep as the ocean and as long as a faraway road. So where do we start? First of all, with “luân thường” – how people should treat each other properly.

dichXuoi.en: We must understand it, because it is the way to be a good person. We learn to be good people – and the very first lesson is “hiếu”, loving and respecting our parents.

en: Cô Hà welcomes you to lesson fourteen of “Lên Tám”. Last time we understood the hard work of parents and teachers and how vast the world of books is. Today she'll show you the best way to start that huge journey of learning. Listen to today's two verses.
Deep as the boundless ocean, far as the long road – where does learning begin? First of all, with “luân thường”.
We must understand “luân thường” – being a good person is the way; we learn how to be good people, and we should begin by knowing “hiếu”.

The poem compares learning to huge things: the ocean so deep you can't see the bottom, a road so long you never reach the end – like humanity's endless knowledge. So where do we start? First with “luân thường”: the basic rules of how people treat each other in the family and society. Letters and maths matter, but learning good manners comes first.

So the poem stresses: understand these rules, because that is the way to be a good person. Why do we go to school? To learn how to be good people. And the very first and most important step is “hiếu” – the root of all goodness. A child who loves and listens to their grandparents and parents can grow into a good citizen. Keep this lesson in your heart.
